segments: The Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
took his wife and his children and fled to the church.
And this Zeno sent and stripped him, his wife, and his children of the royal purples,
and gave them his word that they would not be killed.
And he sent them to Limnae, a fortress of Cappadocia,
and they were imprisoned in one of the towers.
And when it was closed up against them,
they died miserably.
And when Zeno was established in the kingdom,
he fulfilled his oath.
And he made the son of Harmatius Caesar,
and commanded that there should be public games {hippodrome?},
and both of them sat [there].
And him [Harmatius] he had exalted with the generalship {magister militum?}.
Then Zeno reflected:
"It is not improbable that if Harmatius becomes powerful,
just as he betrayed Basiliscus,
he may also dig a pit for me."
Therefore he said:
"Behold, I have fulfilled what I swore;
henceforth let Harmatius die, who transgressed the oath made with Basiliscus."
And when he had killed Harmatius,
he tonsured his son and made him a lector;
and afterwards he commanded and he became metropolitan of the Hellespont, which is Cyzicus.
And this [merely] because he had been deemed worthy to wear the royal purples! And in the ninth year of Zeno, Balash reigned over the Persians for four years.
And in his eleventh year,
Qawad, son of Peroz, reigned after Balash for eleven years.
And in the days of Zeno, the Samaritans rebelled and set up as king over themselves a certain Justa.
And he killed a great number of Christians,
and entered Caesarea {OCR?},
and burned the church of Procopius.
And the Romans of Palestine gathered together,
and fought and defeated the Samaritans,
and sent the head of their king to Zeno.
And the king commanded,
and turned the synagogue of the Samaritans into a great church for Saint Marina (or Mary).
And in Antioch, too, they burned the synagogue of the Jews,
and many of the Jews,
and they also burned the bones of their dead in the graves.
And after these things, this Zeno fell into a bowel disease and died.
